question: Does the Orozco and Zafaralla (2012) citation in the Makati Public Rail EIS support reported fish occurrences in Pasig River?

citationTrace.citingSource: The 2019 Makati Public Rail EIS Table 2-31 labels its table ‘Reported Species in Pasig River’ and attributes Rasbora maculata and Anabas testudineus to Orozco & Zafaralla (2012).

exact2012Source.title: Biophysico-Chemical and Socioeconomic Study of Two Major Manila Esteros
exact2012Source.citation: Orozco, G. P., & Zafaralla, M. T. (2012). In Biology Education for Social and Sustainable Development, pp. 161–171. SensePublishers. DOI: 10.1007/978-94-6091-927-5_17.
exact2012Source.fullTextStatus: The Springer landing page exposes metadata and abstract, but the chapter is subscription content; full chapter not retrieved.

related2008Record.title: Preliminary physico-chemical and fish survey of two esteros in Manila City
related2008Record.citation: Orozco, G. P., Zafaralla, M., & Flavier, M. (2008). Philippine Biota, 41(2). DLSU Animo Repository record 9122.
related2008Record.fullTextStatus: The repository record supplies metadata and abstract, and reports that the upload is unavailable.

citationTrace.lineageDecision: The two records share authors, the same two named esteros, and the same four fish names in their abstracts. Treat them as a related research lineage until full texts establish whether they are overlapping or independent datasets; do not double-count them as separate surveys.

stationScope.2008Article: The abstract reports five sampling stations across the two esteros.
stationScope.2012Chapter: The abstract describes both esteros and seasonal/station comparisons.
stationScope.speciesToStationCrosswalk: Not available in the reviewed metadata/abstracts. No species-to-estero or species-to-station assignment is inferred.

localityAndTaxonomyFindings.localityDecision: The directly cited chapter identifies Estero de San Miguel and Estero de Quiapo, not Pasig River, as its study waterbodies. Its abstract does not establish a Pasig capture or occurrence for Rasbora maculata or Anabas testudineus.

sourceTableComparison.name: Rasbora maculata
sourceTableComparison.independent source finding: The 2008 and 2012 abstracts report the taxon in the two esteros, without a station assignment.
sourceTableComparison.decision: Keep as a two-estero research lead; do not assign it to Pasig River from the EIS citation.

sourceTableComparison.name: Anabas testudineus
sourceTableComparison.independent source finding: The 2008 and 2012 abstracts report the taxon in the two esteros, without a station assignment.
sourceTableComparison.decision: Keep as a two-estero research lead; do not assign it to Pasig River from the EIS citation.

sourceTableComparison.name: Hypostomus plecostomus
sourceTableComparison.EIS attribution: Not listed under this name in the EIS Table 2-31; the EIS instead has a separate Chanos chanos/Hypophthalmichthys nobilis washout note and two source-spelled Pterygoplychthys labels.
sourceTableComparison.independent source finding: Reported in both Orozco/Zafaralla abstracts as one of four estero fish taxa.
sourceTableComparison.decision: Do not use this estero record to silently correct or synonymize any EIS Pasig fish label.

localityAndTaxonomyFindings.sourceScopeWarning: The phrase ‘Manila esteros’ and broad city/river-system context do not transform an Estero de San Miguel or Estero de Quiapo record into a Pasig River station record. Hydraulic connectivity, if any, is not a fish locality crosswalk.

evidenceLimits.dates: The 2008 record says October 2008 publication; a field collection date is not shown in the reviewed abstract. The 2012 record gives publication year, not a fish-specific collection date.
evidenceLimits.methods: The 2008 repository abstract calls the work a fish survey and reports five stations, but does not expose fish gear, effort, identification procedure, or station-level catch data. The 2012 abstract does not expose a fish-to-station matrix.
evidenceLimits.vouchers: No voucher/catalog identifiers or specimen repository records found in the reviewed pages.
evidenceLimits.rights: No open license was identified on the Springer chapter or DLSU repository page; full text was unavailable. No table, image, or article text is reproduced here.

nextActions: Keep the Orozco/Zafaralla taxa assigned only to the source's two esteros at an aggregated research level unless full text supplies a defensible station crosswalk.
Seek the full 2008 article and 2012 chapter, then compare methods, dates, stations, and overlap before counting the lineage as one or more surveys.
Keep the Makati EIS Table 2-31 as a mixed, non-station-resolved reported list; its other taxa still need their own source tracing.
